To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nurse administrators in Georgia are not fully utilizing existing clinical guidelines to assure an adequate quality of care and to mentor the staff nurses.
there were no organized procedures for evaluating nurse managers in Georgia, and that many of them viewed financial constraints as obstacles for delivering better quality nursing care.
nurse administrators in the country of Georgia are not practicing at the level of the International Council for Nurses (ICN) competencies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of nursing care and the safety of patients and nurses in the Republic of the Georgia.
the development of effective nursing management practices to improve the quality of nursing care in a resource constrained environment.
the need to improve the competencies of nurse administrators to provide quality health care to the Georgian people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nurse administrators in Georgia need to improve their knowledge and skill levels to provide quality care in their respective settings and to be able to mentor staff nurses.

nurse managers are not fully prepared to manage the nursing workforce in the Republic of the Georgia and the Republic of Georgia is not fully prepared to support nurse administrators to effectively manage the nursing workforce.
nurse administrators in Georgia are in need of additional education in order to meet the international standards of nursing management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nursing profession is in a state of transition in Georgia.
we have developed a framework for nurse managers to improve the quality of nursing care in a resource-constrained environment.
nurse administrators should not be expected to perform at an optimal level without adequate resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nurse administrators in the developing country context are in a unique position to influence change and to advocate for the nursing profession.

nurse administrators can play a vital role in improving nursing care delivery in resource-limited settings by implementing evidence-based practice guidelines and by ensuring a safe work place for nurses and other staff members.
nurse managers in Georgia have the potential to be excellent nurse administrators. However, they need support and guidance from the government and from international organizations.
